pubcol-w-25dd2bc4850f5550.definition_en: the practice of organising and planning how to divide your time between different tasks
pubcol-w-25dd2bc4850f5550.example_simple: Good time-management helps me finish my homework before dinner.
pubcol-w-25dd2bc4850f5550.example_complex: Effective time-management is often the difference between employees who thrive under pressure and those who feel constantly overwhelmed.

f530b061-96c2-4751-8f02-b78f44c34c2b.definition_en: a long, angry speech criticising someone or something

145474e0-5ee2-4d6c-87b3-a3d0c869fe93.definition_en: an abnormal enlargement of body tissue, usually caused by injury, infection or fluid build-up

pubcol-w-d2087ce58df44951.definition_en: in a dangerous situation where failure, loss or harm is likely
pubcol-w-d2087ce58df44951.example_simple: The heavy rain put the whole trip in jeopardy.
pubcol-w-d2087ce58df44951.example_complex: One careless email had placed the entire merger in jeopardy, and the board scrambled to reassure their nervous investors.

pubcol-w-9dbde0c943ccc969.example_simple: To some degree, I agree with you, but I still have doubts.
pubcol-w-9dbde0c943ccc969.example_complex: Her success can be attributed to talent, but to a degree it also reflects the many opportunities she was fortunate enough to receive.

pubcol-w-c58d7b4d775d3f33.definition_en: unable to think what to say or do; confused and uncertain
collocations: be at a loss for words
pubcol-w-c58d7b4d775d3f33.example_simple: When she asked me such a difficult question, I was at a loss for words.
pubcol-w-c58d7b4d775d3f33.example_complex: Faced with the sudden collapse of the project, even the senior managers were at a loss to explain what had gone so badly wrong.

pubcol-w-d6edc06b53c9dfe5.definition_en: to be certain or obliged to do something
pubcol-w-d6edc06b53c9dfe5.example_simple: If you keep practising, you are bound to improve.
pubcol-w-d6edc06b53c9dfe5.example_complex: Given the mounting pressure from shareholders, the company was bound to announce redundancies sooner or later.

pubcol-w-1c6be98e3f060c60.ipa: /tə bi ɪn ðə muːd fər ə ˌhəʊm kʊkt miːl/
pubcol-w-1c6be98e3f060c60.definition_en: to feel like eating a meal prepared at home rather than eating out
collocations: in the mood for something light
pubcol-w-1c6be98e3f060c60.example_simple: After a long week, I'm in the mood for a home-cooked meal instead of takeaway.
pubcol-w-1c6be98e3f060c60.example_complex: Exhausted from months of business travel and restaurant food, she was suddenly in the mood for a simple home-cooked meal with her family.

pubcol-w-05a955998d5e509c.definition_en: to lose your job because your employer no longer needs your role
pubcol-w-05a955998d5e509c.example_simple: He was made redundant when the factory closed down.
pubcol-w-05a955998d5e509c.example_complex: Thousands of workers were made redundant as the company shifted its production overseas to cut costs.

pubcol-w-09e6e9c132a0c7c4.definition_en: to be available to support and help someone when they need it
collocations: be there for someone in need
pubcol-w-09e6e9c132a0c7c4.example_simple: Whenever I have a problem, my best friend is always there for me.
pubcol-w-09e6e9c132a0c7c4.example_complex: Even after moving to another country, she made sure her ageing parents knew she would always be there for them.

pubcol-w-7c35508bfa435c1c.definition_en: to do something wrong without being caught or punished for it
pubcol-w-7c35508bfa435c1c.example_simple: He thought he could get away with lying, but his teacher noticed.
pubcol-w-7c35508bfa435c1c.example_complex: For years the executives got away with falsifying the accounts, until an internal auditor finally exposed the fraud.

pubcol-w-0781d060c85db0a4.definition_en: to start giving your serious attention to something
pubcol-w-0781d060c85db0a4.example_simple: Let's stop chatting and get down to work.
pubcol-w-0781d060c85db0a4.example_complex: Once the introductions were over, the negotiators finally got down to the difficult business of agreeing on a price.

pubcol-w-4276dad663e4335c.definition_en: to climb onto or board a bus, train, plane or bicycle
pubcol-w-4276dad663e4335c.example_simple: We got on the bus just before it left the station.
pubcol-w-4276dad663e4335c.example_complex: As the last passengers hurried to get on the crowded train, the doors slid shut and the platform emptied.

pubcol-w-44041189707f3a86.definition_en: to recall something precisely and accurately
pubcol-w-44041189707f3a86.example_simple: I read the poem many times so that I could remember it exactly.
pubcol-w-44041189707f3a86.example_complex: Although the incident happened years ago, she could still remember it exactly, down to the colour of the sky that afternoon.

pubcol-w-24b045223337b149.ipa: /tə ˈsentəns ˌsʌmbədi tə ə ˈlaɪftaɪm ɪmˈprɪzənmənt/
pubcol-w-24b045223337b149.definition_en: to officially punish someone with imprisonment for the rest of their life
pubcol-w-24b045223337b149.example_simple: The judge decided to sentence the man to lifetime imprisonment for the crime.
pubcol-w-24b045223337b149.example_complex: After a lengthy trial, the court chose to sentence the offender to lifetime imprisonment, ruling that he posed a permanent danger to the public.

pubcol-w-9b7cd12dbdfd91d2.ipa: /tə ˈsʌmbədi huː ɪz ˈstɑːtɪŋ ə ˈdʒɜːni/
pubcol-w-9b7cd12dbdfd91d2.definition_en: addressed or offered to a person who is beginning a new venture or journey
collocations: advice to someone starting a journey
a gift for someone starting a journey
pubcol-w-9b7cd12dbdfd91d2.example_simple: This little book of tips is meant for somebody who is starting a journey.
pubcol-w-9b7cd12dbdfd91d2.example_complex: The professor dedicated her farewell speech to somebody who is starting a journey, offering hard-won wisdom to every graduate about to leave the campus.
pubcol-w-9b7cd12dbdfd91d2.vi_meaning_correction: (gửi) tới người sắp bắt đầu một hành trình mới

pubcol-w-daac5c72cd942e8e.definition_en: as far as I know; according to what I believe to be true
collocations: to the best of my knowledge and belief
to the best of my recollection
state to the best of my knowledge
pubcol-w-daac5c72cd942e8e.example_simple: To the best of my knowledge, the shop closes at six o'clock.
pubcol-w-daac5c72cd942e8e.example_complex: To the best of my knowledge, no such agreement was ever signed, though I cannot rule out discussions I was not party to.

pubcol-w-aea5c5cddf5ea491.definition_en: with this meaning or purpose; conveying this idea
pubcol-w-aea5c5cddf5ea491.example_simple: She said she was too busy, or something to this effect.
pubcol-w-aea5c5cddf5ea491.example_complex: The minister issued a formal statement to this effect, insisting that no further concessions would be made during the negotiations.
pubcol-w-aea5c5cddf5ea491.vi_meaning_correction: với ý nghĩa/nội dung như thế này

pubcol-w-2b0440f17fd0a00d.definition_en: to get rid of something you no longer want, or to waste an opportunity
pubcol-w-2b0440f17fd0a00d.example_simple: Please don't throw away those old newspapers; I want to recycle them.
pubcol-w-2b0440f17fd0a00d.example_complex: By turning down the scholarship, he threw away an opportunity that most students could only dream of.

pubcol-w-801e370b2415b7aa.definition_en: to add something extra, or to contribute a remark to a conversation
pubcol-w-801e370b2415b7aa.example_simple: The salesman threw in a free case when I bought the phone.
pubcol-w-801e370b2415b7aa.example_complex: Whenever the debate grew tense, she would throw in a light-hearted remark to ease the atmosphere.

pubcol-w-5a0586d5690ff24e.definition_en: to get rid of something troublesome, or to escape from someone following you
pubcol-w-5a0586d5690ff24e.example_simple: It took me a week to throw off that nasty cold.
pubcol-w-5a0586d5690ff24e.example_complex: The fugitive changed cars twice in an effort to throw off the detectives who had been tailing him for days.

pubcol-w-febe662f9a496846.definition_en: to get rid of something unwanted, or to reject an idea or proposal
pubcol-w-febe662f9a496846.example_simple: We need to throw out all this broken furniture.
pubcol-w-febe662f9a496846.example_complex: The committee threw out the original plan, arguing that it was far too expensive to implement.
